correctness.rationale: The labelled Gaussian/Hermite spectral formula is established in the primary radial localization literature. Direct sign-change polynomial separation proves global injectivity for two at-most-m annular masks. The endpoint Jacobian is exactly a signed exponential Vandermonde and is nowhere singular in the strict chamber; its (2m-1)-row truncation has rank 2m-1, producing sharp local ambiguity by the implicit function theorem. An explicit Lagrange inverse derivative and 70-digit checker independently test normalizations and finite cases. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

None inspected states the complete sharp finite Hermite-indexed endpoint identification including every-point lower bound and explicit conditioning. Possible specialist moment-problem equivalences are a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: General Chebyshev-system moment inversion or fixed-amplitude spike literature might already imply a mathematically equivalent 2m-moment identification; specialist exhaustive historical priority was not independently certified.
Literature searches are not proofs of first publication; same result may be phrased without localization or Hermite terminology.
A global stable solver and unordered spectrum reconstruction are not provided.

value.rationale: The exact minimum number of physically meaningful Hermite probes to identify a general m-ring binary phase-space mask is determined, including global uniqueness, a local one-dimensional obstruction below the bound at every mask, and an explicit endpoint sensitivity formula. This is a natural tight inverse spectral design benchmark rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
